title: Midcycle SKU Swap Playbook and Regional Canary Plan
content:
Purpose:
This note captures a pragmatic runbook for performing a midcycle SKU swap across the fleet when upstream lead-times, price moves, or urgent capacity needs make the originally committed SKU suboptimal. Focus is on minimizing customer impact, preserving SLAs, and keeping finance and sales aligned.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to reserved orders and committed replenishment windows (0–90 day horizon).
- Target is GPU class swaps where compatibility is high (same compute family / similar memory profile) — not wholesale architecture migrations.
- Swap can be unilateral (we change incoming PO SKU) or symmetric (we swap some arriving racks for a different SKU and adjust placement).
- We assume Private/Dedicated customers pinned to exact SKUs will be treated by a separate escalation flow.

Signals that trigger a midcycle swap: (examples)
- Vendor notifies delay > 2 weeks and regional burn rate exceeds runway threshold.
- Spot market or reseller offers a high-confidence immediate delivery (<=3 weeks) at similar TCO.
- New SKU gives >=15% throughput improvement for specific hot workloads (inference cost wins).
- Pricing delta > 20% and finance recommends hedging.

Quick decision heuristics (checklist):
- Is the swap compatible with our runtime (driver/kernel validated)? (Ops)
- Does the swap require additional cooling/pdu/space changes? (Infra)
- Are there production customers pinned to exact SKU in the affected region? (CS/Legal)
- Is the financial delta +/- material for committed contracts? (Finance)
- Do we have validated perf numbers for our top 10 models? (Applied ML)
- Lead time delta: immediate availability (<=21 days) preferred.

Roles & escalation matrix:
- On-call procurement lead: Jonah Li — primary for vendor negotiation and PO edits.
- Fleet ops lead: Priya Shah — coordinates staging, image compatibility, and QA canaries.
- SRE/Runtime: Lena Ortiz — validates runtime/kernel behavior and rollout gating.
- PMR/Customer success liaison: assigned per affected accounts — triggers customer comms.
- Finance approval: required for swaps altering committed spend >$250k per quarter.

Pre-swap validation steps (can run in parallel):
1) Inventory and arrival window check (Procurement): confirm shipments that can be swapped without incurring cancellation penalties.
2) Compatibility smoke tests (Runtime): quick driver boot, nv_gpu health check, kv-cache sanity. Maintain a short checklist script in tools/smoke-scripts (link in linked_artifacts).
3) Performance delta validation (Applied ML): run 1–2 synthetic microbenchmarks for our top generator and embedding workloads — aim for <48 hour feedback. Use the controlled bench cluster.
4) Power/space check (Facilities): validate racks will accept swapped SKU (TDP, connectors).
5) Billing/commit check (Finance): produce a delta P&L (3–12 month horizon) and surface to procurement.

Risk categories and mitigations:
- Firmware/kernel incompatibility: mitigation = short canary fleet (1 rack per region) for 72h, fallback plan to original SKU in staging.
- Customer SLA regressions: pre-notify customers >72h before planned swap if pins present; automatic fallback policy for pinned workflows.
- Vendor cancellation fees: quantify penalty threshold and compare to runway risk cost. If penalty < 50% of runway shortfall cost, proceed with swap.

Regional canary rollout plan (example timeline):
- Day 0: Procurement edits PO or accepts incoming reseller shipment. Inform finance and legal.
- Day 1–2: Staging (1 rack) in west-us-west1 — run smoke tests, kernel profile capture, perf bench.
- Day 3: Expand canary to two additional racks; run continuous inference workload for 24h.
- Day 4–5: If stable, schedule staggered inbound placement (1 region at a time) with per-region telemetry checks.
- Day 6–14: Monitor per-region SLO dashboards and token-level latency/cost metrics. Abort window for rollbacks is Day 6.

Ops runbook (step-by-step):
- Step A: Open a "SKU swap" ticket (prefix: infra-swap-YYYYMMDD) and tag on-call procurement & ops.
- Step B: Attach PO changes and vendor confirmation to ticket.
- Step C: Provision a canary rack in staging with image vX.y (same as prod), apply driver package vZ.
content_continued:
- Step D: Run smoke checklist: boot, nvidia-smi, run model microbench (30s sample), check kernel logs for OOM/page faults.
- Step E: If smoke pass, kick off perf harness (30–90 min) and compare against baseline. Save artifacts to /artifacts/sku-swap/YYYYMMDD.
- Step F: Tag results in the ticket and notify CS for any pinned accounts.
- Step G: If canary green, schedule staggered placement windows by region (prefer low-traffic windows).
- Step H: Post-placement validation: run synthetic production traffic for 4h, then allow live traffic with a 15% traffic ramp for 6h, then full return.
- Step I: If regression detected (>5% P95 latency increase or >3% error rate), trigger rollback playbook.

Rollback playbook (fast):
- Revert placement using inbound inventory of original SKU if available.
- If inbound original SKU not available, reprovision capacity in other regions not yet swapped and re-route traffic.
- Notify legal/finance of any contract exposure and start mitigation conversation.

Open questions / TODOs:
- (TODO) Automation: add a single-click PO-edit flag in procurement UI to mark swap-eligible POs (owner: Jonah).
- (Research) Quantify the acceptable penalty threshold functionally rather than ad-hoc (owner: Finance).
- (Ops) Create a nightly job to compute real-time runway per region and surface exposures.

Example numeric run (illustrative):
- Region: eu-west2
- Current inbound: 4 racks of SKU-A, ETA 35 days
- Alternative immediate: 2 racks SKU-B available in 10 days, 2 racks SKU-C available in 18 days
- Burn rate: 0.35 racks/day -> runway = 11.5 days (critical)
Decision path: since runway < ETA and SKU-B provides immediate partial coverage, we accept SKU-B for first 2 racks and push remaining 2 racks to reseller offer for SKU-C.

Metrics to track post-swap (dashboards to update):
- Per-region runway (days) — critical flag < 14 days
- Percent of fleet swapped (by SKU)
- 99 PCT tail latency delta per model cohort
- Token cost delta per million tokens (finance)
- Vendor penalty totals (if any)

Communication templates (short):
- Internal Slack (ops channel): "Planned SKU swap for eu-west2: 2 racks SKU-A -> SKU-B. Canary tonight at 22:00 UTC. Tagging @oncall-procurement @oncall-ops."
- Customer facing (if pinned): "Hi <Customer>, we plan a hardware intake update in <region> to avoid capacity shortage. No expected impact to your service; we will monitor and notify if anything changes. Contact: <CS rep>."
Notes to self (informal):
- Keep swaps preferentially within same chip-family to reduce kernel variance.
- Avoid swapping if new SKU requires significant cooling or PDU rework (>1 rack-level change).
- Try to batch small swaps across adjacent regions to reduce cross-region cold-start churn.

Appendix: small helper table (heuristic thresholds)

Threshold | Action
---------|-------
Runway < 14d and ETA > runway +7d | Trigger immediate swap evaluation
Perf delta >= 15% throughput | High-priority swap candidate
Price delta >= 20% | Finance to re-evaluate; consider swap if bulk savings > cancellation penalty
Penalty < 50% of runway loss cost | Accept penalty and swap

References and bookmarks:
- Confluence: procurement playbook (linked_artifacts)
- JIRA: INFRA-872 (linked_artifacts)
- Slack: #infra-procurement (linked_artifacts)

End of draft — feedback welcome.
